question: The Commission has recently adopted safeguard measures on the imports of certain ferroalloying elements, citing serious injury or threat thereof to EU producers.

Regulation (EU) No 978/20121 establishing the Generalised Scheme of Preferences provides that imports originating in countries benefiting from the Everything But Arms (EBA) arrangement enjoy duty-free and quota-free access to the EU market, except where safeguard or other restrictive measures are expressly applied. In this context, could the Commission clarify: 1.
Whether the newly adopted safeguard measures on ferro-alloying elements apply to imports originating in countries benefiting from the EBA arrangement?

If so, what is the legal basis for the inclusion of EBA beneficiary countries within the scope of these measures, and have there been any exemptions, derogations, or differentiated treatment are provided for under Regulation (EU) No 978/2012?

How will the Commission ensure that the application of these safeguard measures is consistent with the EU’s development policy objectives, as well as with its obligations under World Trade Organization rules.
OJ L 303, 31.10.2012, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2012/978/oj.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.2.

2026) The safeguard measures on certain ferro-alloying elements were adopted1 under the EU’s general safeguard framework (Regulation (EU) 2015/4782 and Regulation (EU) 2015/7553) and implemented in full conformity with World Trade Organisation (WTO) safeguard rules: safeguard measures are global in scope and apply to imports from all third countries, regardless of preferential arrangements.
Beneficiary countries under the Everything But Arms (EBA) arrangement4 are therefore not subject to a special treatment nor automatically excluded from the measures because of their EBA status.

However, in compliance with the WTO safeguards agreement5, developing countries are exempted from a safeguard measure if their individual import share does not exceed 3%, provided that developing country members of the WTO with less than a 3% import share collectively account for no more than 9% of total EU imports.

This balanced approach aims to protect EU’s industry while supporting the development and economic integration of least-developed countries, in line with WTO law. While Regulation (EU) 978/20126 governs Generalised Scheme of Preferences and EBA preferences, it does not prevent the EU from adopting safeguard measures of general application where the relevant legal conditions are fulfilled.

Regulation (EU) 978/2012 also provides for special safeguards rules, which do not constitute a trade defence instrument or a safeguard measure within the meaning of Regulations (EU) 2015/478 and (EU) 2015/755, nor a safeguard measure within the meaning of the WTO Agreement on Safeguards7, pursuant to Article XIX of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade 1994.

1 http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg_impl/2025/2351/oj. 2 http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2015/478/oj. 3 http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2015/755/oj. 4 https://gsphub.eu/about-gsp/eba. 5 As transposed by Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2015/478 (please see footnote 2). 6 http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2012/978/oj. 7 https://www.wto.org/english/res_e/publications_e/ai17_e/safeguards_e.htm.
